correctness.rationale: For every successor u of w, transitivity and Euclideanness give R(u)=R(w), with no finite-frame assumption. Consequently the truth of each formula depends inductively only on its current atom valuation and that common successor valuation support. For a singleton support every Δ formula at the point is true regardless of the singleton valuation. For a nonsingleton support, negated Δ of the minterm for b holds precisely when b is in the support, so such supports cannot collapse further. Combining these tests and root literals defines every profile, and Boolean closure defines every subset of the m(2^m−m) profiles. A reflexive cluster with one world per support valuation realizes each required successor support; add an external root only if its valuation is not represented. In that event the support is proper, so |S|+1≤m. The singleton class also admits a one-world realization. The conjunction of negated Δ of all valuation minterms forces every valuation to occur among successors when k≥1, giving a sharp m-world requirement. For Box, testing all valuation minterms with possibility distinguishes every nonempty support, giving the comparison census. An independent finite refinement of formula truth classes on all 442 pointed one-atom models on up to three labelled worlds (/workspace/audit_replay_2.py) stabilized at four Δ theories and six Box theories. The proof, not the finite test, covers all k and infinite frames.

value.rationale: The world cutoff gives an optimal finite witness size for satisfiability and for the failure of semantic equivalence in a standard belief logic, including satisfiability initially witnessed on infinite frames. The profile proof explains exactly what information is lost by using non-contingency instead of necessity despite the presence of cycles. This utility is distinct from the earlier terminal-star question-count optimization; the repeated numerical census alone would add little.
